title: Part (1) final answer
description: Essential: The response must give the correct expression for the initial velocity, derived from energy conservation: v0 = sqrt(2eU0/m).

title: Part (2) final answer
description: Essential: The response must give the correct expression for the initial velocity, derived from magnetic circular motion: v0 = e B0 R / (2m).

title: Part (3) final answer
description: Essential: The response must give the correct expression for the total kinetic energy per unit length per unit time: Ek = π R e a b p² / (m I).

title: Energy conservation in (1)
description: Important: The solution must apply the work-energy theorem, equating the initial kinetic energy to the work done by the electric field.

title: Circular motion in (2)
description: Important: The solution must recognize that the maximum radius of the electron's helical/circular path is R/2 and equate the Lorentz force to the centripetal force.

title: Electron flux calculation
description: Important: For part (3), the solution must correctly relate the measured current I to the number of electrons hitting the plate per unit time, using geometry (fraction a/(2πR)).

title: Pressure-momentum relation
description: Important: For part (3), the solution must apply the momentum theorem (pressure = force/area) to relate pressure p to the electron's momentum and flux.

title: Sign or direction error
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the sign of the electron charge (e) is incorrectly handled in the Lorentz force or energy equations, leading to a wrong expression.

title: Geometric misinterpretation
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the radius of the circular path in part (2) is incorrectly taken as R instead of R/2, or if the fraction of electrons hitting the plate in part (3) is wrong.

title: Unit consistency check
description: Optional: The solution may include a verification that the final expressions for v0 and Ek have the correct physical dimensions (e.g., velocity, energy/(length·time)).
